questions.question: How does a family most often get money?
options: They find it on the ground in the park
They get it for free from the accountant
They simply have money
From adults working – a salary or wages
questions.explanation: A family most often gets money from the work of adults. When parents work, they receive a salary or payment for their work.

questions.question: Chrumko notices that mom is looking at a message from the bank on her phone. What happened?
options: Nothing happened, the bank just writes sometimes
Mom received her paycheck for work
Dad bought a baguette
It's always a problem
questions.explanation: Mom received her paycheck – money she gets for her work. It arrived in her bank account.

questions.question: What is money used for?
options: For rent, groceries and school supplies
Only for toys and sweets
It's completely useless, swapping goods for goods works fine
It's never needed
questions.explanation: With this money the family pays for rent, groceries and school supplies.

questions.question: Money appears in a household by itself, even if the parents don't work.
questions.explanation: Money comes into the family because parents work and receive payment for it.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Parents receive a salary for their work.
Family money comes exclusively from gifts.
Some parents run their own business and earn money in their own company.
questions.explanation: Most family money comes from work. Gifts and benefits are only other sources.

questions.question: Match the source of money with the correct description.
matchRight: Money the family receives as a gift
Regular payment from an employer for work
questions.explanation: A family can get money from several sources, but most often from work.

questions.question: Place each source of money into the correct group.
questions.explanation: Money for work is the main source. Gifts and benefits are other sources.

questions.question: Put in order how Chrumko gradually understands where money in the family comes from.
orderItems: Chrumko notices that mom is looking at a message from the bank
Mom explains to him that she received her paycheck for work
Mom shows him that this money pays for rent, groceries and school supplies
Chrumko understands that household money comes from the parents' work
questions.explanation: Chrumko gradually understands the relationship between work and money in the family.

questions.question: What are household expenses?
options: Only what we buy in a shop with cash
Only big purchases, such as a car
All the money that needs to be paid for the home to function
The family's property that is kept at home in a piggy bank
questions.explanation: Household expenses are all the money that needs to be paid for the home to function – for example housing, food, utilities or internet.

questions.question: Chrumko wonders why his parents didn't buy a new decorative flowerpot. What does dad show him?
options: That they have enough money for everything
That this week they already paid the bill for internet, water and school lunches
That they have no money at all
That they already have enough flowerpots at home
questions.explanation: This week they already had other expenses. Even though these aren't big things, together they add up to a larger sum.

questions.question: Money leaves the household only for big purchases.
questions.explanation: Money often goes out on many small, necessary payments that add up together.

questions.question: Match each expense with its category.
questions.explanation: A household pays for housing, food, utilities, transport and other things.

questions.question: Place household expenses into the correct groups.
questions.explanation: A family has to budget for utilities, housing and food.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: A household doesn't have to pay for water and electricity.
Household expenses include rent, food and utilities.
Even small payments add up to a larger sum.
questions.explanation: Water and electricity are utilities that a household pays for regularly.

questions.question: Why does a family's money disappear even when they don't buy anything big?
options: Parents lose the money
Everything in the shop is very expensive
Bills aren't paid regularly, and that's why they are very expensive
Many small necessary payments are made, which together add up to a larger sum
questions.explanation: Even small regular payments (internet, water, lunches) add up together.

questions.question: Why do we pay for housing even though we already live in the apartment?
options: There's no reason to pay when we already live in the apartment
Everything about housing is free
Housing also means heating, water, common areas and maintenance, which cost money
You pay only once when moving in, and after that water, electricity and internet are always free
questions.explanation: Housing isn't just the space itself. It also includes heating, water, common areas and maintenance.

questions.question: A home needs constant care and maintenance, which cost money.
questions.explanation: When something breaks, it needs to be fixed, and that costs money.

questions.question: Match each item with the correct description.
matchRight: Regular payment for using an apartment
Regular payment for buying a house
questions.explanation: Housing requires regular payments, services and repairs.

questions.question: Place items into the correct groups of housing expenses.
questions.explanation: A home costs money regularly and also when something breaks.

questions.question: Chrumko's mom says that when the elevator breaks or the roof needs repairing, it costs money. What does that mean?
options: Home maintenance and repairs cost money too
The roof and elevator get fixed overnight
Repairs are always free
You pay for housing only once
questions.explanation: A home needs constant care, and that costs money.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Rent is a regular payment for housing.
Heating and water are part of housing costs.
Repairs and home maintenance never cost any money.
questions.explanation: Repairs and maintenance are part of housing costs.

questions.question: Put in order how Chrumko learns about housing costs.
orderItems: Chrumko hears his parents talking about monthly payments for the apartment
He asks why they pay for a place they already have
Mom explains to him that housing also means heating, water, common areas and maintenance
Chrumko understands that a home needs constant care
questions.explanation: Chrumko gradually understands that housing costs money.

questions.question: Why doesn't the refrigerator fill itself with food?
options: Food grows at home right in the fridge
Groceries get used up and need to be bought regularly
The fridge is magical, so whenever food runs out, it conjures more
Food is free, you take it from the shop, not buy it
questions.explanation: Food gets used up, so it needs to be replenished often.

questions.question: Chrumko goes on a small shopping trip with mom. What do they put in the cart?
options: Bread, milk, fruit, cheese, pasta and yogurts
Only toys and sweets
Nothing, the fridge conjures everything at home
Everything they see, because goods are free
questions.explanation: It seems to Chrumko that they're buying only a few things, but at the checkout the total is higher than he expected.

questions.question: Food is a large, regular part of a family's expenses.
questions.explanation: Food is among the biggest regular expenses of every family.

questions.question: Match each situation with what follows from it.
matchLeft: At the checkout after shopping, the total is
matchRight: More food and a higher expense
It needs to be replenished often
questions.explanation: Food is a large regular part of expenses.

questions.question: Place the statements into the correct group.
dragLabels: Food gets used up and needs to be replenished
A larger family needs more food
questions.explanation: Food gets used up and costs money, so it needs to be bought regularly.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Food gets used up and needs to be replenished often.
A family doesn't need to buy food, because the fridge fills itself.
Small items add up to a large monthly sum.
questions.explanation: The fridge doesn't fill itself – food needs to be bought regularly.

questions.question: Why is the total at the checkout often higher than we expected?
options: The cashier always makes a mistake and counts everything several times
Mom bought only one expensive item
The amount we pay depends on the time we spend in the shop
Even everyday groceries cost quite a lot together, small items add up
questions.explanation: Even everyday groceries cost quite a lot together, which is why food is a large regular expense.

questions.question: Why do parents turn off the light when we don't need it?
options: Because they have lights that are too strong at home
Light is free, but they simply decided to turn it off anyway
Because electricity and water cost money
It never makes sense
questions.explanation: Even small things add up over the month.

questions.question: Chrumko leaves his room and leaves the light on. What does mom do?
options: Leaves it on, energy is free after all
Calls Chrumko back to turn off the light
She doesn't care, she gets a high salary from work
She loves Chrumko, so she says nothing
questions.explanation: Mom explains to him that even small things add up over the month.

questions.question: Energy is invisible, and therefore it costs no money.
questions.explanation: Energy isn't visible like an object, but it costs money every day.

questions.question: Match each action with its effect.
matchLeft: Turning off water while brushing teeth
Fridge left open for a long time
questions.explanation: Small habits save or waste money.

questions.question: Sort the actions by whether they save energy or waste it.
dragLabels: Turning off water while brushing teeth
Turning off the light in an empty room
Leaving the fridge open for a long time
questions.explanation: Small habits over time turn into bigger savings or costs.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Energy is free and we don't need to think about it.
Electricity and water are services that must be paid for.
Small things, like turning off a light, add up over the month.
questions.explanation: Energy must be paid for and its consumption adds up over the month.

questions.question: Put in order how Chrumko learns that energy costs money.
orderItems: Chrumko leaves his room and leaves the light on
Mom calls him back and explains that even small things add up over a month
Chrumko understands that energy costs money every day
questions.explanation: He gradually understands how energy consumption adds up.

questions.question: How can family members help reduce energy expenses?
options: Turn off the light when leaving a room
Turn off water while brushing teeth
Switch devices off instead of leaving them on standby
All of the above
questions.explanation: All family members can contribute to saving energy and water.
